claim: PLYFLD = 0x400 (hex; 1024 decimal). The playfield RAM is 30 cells WIDE by 32 HIGH, occupying 0x400-0x7BF (960 bytes = 30*32). Radix is hex (inherited .RADIX 16 from CENDE4), so 400 is 0x400, not decimal 400.

corroboration.note: MAME cabinet ROT270 — the 30-wide x 32-high playfield RAM is mounted on a vertically rotated monitor. Addressing convention: the vertical screen index v = addr & 0x1F (0-31, 32 HIGH); the horizontal index h = (addr - 0x400) >> 5 (0-29, 30 WIDE). v=0x1F is the top (score) row, v=0,1 the bottom (player) rows.

claim: MUSH is the running count of mushrooms on the LOWER part of the screen (the flea-spawn / player zone). It is a per-player 2-byte cell.

source.verbatim: MUSH:	.BLKB 2			;NUMBER OF MUSHROOMS ON LOWER PART OF SCREEN

claim: MEM is the 2-byte playfield ADDRESS POINTER the RESTOR sweep walks while restoring mushrooms after the player's death. MEM+1 == 0 means the sweep is idle/done.

source.verbatim: MEM:	.BLKB 2			;PLAYFIELD ADDRESS POINTER FOR RESTORING MUSHROOMS.

claim: INIT clears the whole playfield (0x400 base) before seeding. The clear loop stamps 0 across PLYFLD, PLYFLD+0x100, +0x200, +0x300 for X=0..0xFF, i.e. 0x400-0x7FF.

Initial mushroom seeding: the column-walk (TEMP1) starts at 0x1B (27 decimal). TEMP1 supplies the low 5 address bits (the vertical index v) of each placement and is DETERMINISTIC — only the row/horizontal bits come from the RNG.

The seeding loop counter is `45.` — the TRAILING PERIOD makes it DECIMAL 45 inside this otherwise-hex file. With the DEX/BPL loop tail (PM-14) this yields 46 placement ATTEMPTS (X = 45 down through 0 inclusive), not 45.

Seeding placement reads RNGEN (the POKEY hardware random-number generator) for the row/horizontal position. This hardware entropy is the ONLY ROM randomness the sim replaces — with the seeded @arcade/shared/rng (mulberry32). The COUNTS, the column walk, the 0x3F value and the reserved rows are ROM facts; the rng stream mapping is adapter policy.

MUSH-count boundary: a placement's vertical index (TEMP2 & 0x1F) compared to 0x0C (12 decimal). At or above 0x0C is the UPPER part of the screen and is NOT counted toward MUSH; below 0x0C is the lower part and IS counted.

corroboration.note: BCS 30$ ;IF ON UPPER PART OF SCREEN — the branch that skips the MUSH increment for v >= 0x0C.

claim: For a lower-screen placement onto an empty cell, MUSH (the lower-screen mushroom count) is incremented by one.

source.verbatim: INC X,MUSH-1		;ADD ONE TO MUSHROOM COUNT

claim: Each seeded obstacle is a FULL mushroom = 0x3F (hex; 63 decimal). The seeding writes 0x3F (EOR CKC0, which is 0 in the upright cabinet).
The full-mushroom value is stamped into the playfield at the computed address (TEMP2).

The column walk stays off the bottom rows: after decrementing TEMP1, if the result is below 2 (0x02) it is NOT used — the walk resets (PM-13). So seeded mushrooms occupy vertical index v in [0x02, 0x1B]; rows v=0 and v=1 (the bottom/player rows) are never seeded.

corroboration.note: BCS 35$ ;STAY OFF BOTTOM ROW — keeps TEMP1 >= 2.

claim: When the column walk would drop below 2 it wraps back to 0x1B (the start), so the deterministic v-sequence cycles through 0x1B..0x02 across the 46 attempts.
The seeding loop tail is DEX / BPL, so with the initial count 45. (decimal, PM-6) it runs 46 times (X = 45 down to 0, then DEX makes -1 and BPL exits). 46 placement attempts total.
When a shot hits an obstacle, its picture is masked to the low 6 bits (& 0x3F) to read the mushroom state.
Mushroom picture codes occupy 0x38-0x3F: a masked value BELOW 0x38 is NOT a mushroom (the shot passes it). So 'is a mushroom' == (cell & 0x3F) >= 0x38.

corroboration.note: BCC 108$ ;IF NOT A MUSHROOM — branch taken for values < 0x38.

claim: A shot DECREMENTS the mushroom picture code by 1 (SBC I,1 with carry set). Full normal mushroom 0x3F steps 0x3F->0x3E->0x3D->0x3C on successive hits.
A NORMAL mushroom (band 0x3C-0x3F) is DESTROYED when the decrement reaches 0x3B — i.e. after 4 shots on a full 0x3F (0x3F->0x3E->0x3D->0x3C->destroyed). MUSHROOM_HP = 4.

corroboration.note: BEQ 106$ ;END OF MUSHROOM — the destroy branch for the normal band.

claim: A POISONED mushroom (band 0x38-0x3B, distinguished from normal by bit 0x04 clear) is DESTROYED when the decrement reaches 0x37 — 4 shots on a full poisoned 0x3B. Both destroy thresholds (0x3B normal, 0x37 poison) prevent a normal mushroom decrementing INTO the poison band.

corroboration.note: BNE 107$ ;NOT END OF MUSHROOM — fall-through to 106$ (destroy) only when the value is 0x37.

claim: DESTROYING a mushroom with a shot awards 1 point (LDA I,01 = 0x01; added in BCD, so 1 point). The point is awarded only on the destroying hit, not on partial hits.
When a shot makes a mushroom disappear, MUSHDC is called to decrement the lower-screen mushroom count.

The RESTOR sweep is ARMED when the player finishes exploding (EXPLOD): MEM is set to 0x0400 (MEM = 0, MEM+1 = 4), i.e. the playfield base. This is why partial/poisoned mushrooms are restored 'after your death'.

corroboration.note: LDA I,4 sets MEM+1 = 0x04; the preceding STA MEM (line 995, after LDA I,0) sets MEM = 0x00 — together MEM = 0x0400 = PLYFLD.

claim: RESTOR is called every frame (JSR RESTOR from MAINLOOP) but does one restore only when FRAME & 0x07 == 0 — i.e. every 8 frames. The adjacent comment 'EVERY 16 FRAMES' is WRONG; the code (AND I,07) wins: cadence is 8 frames.

corroboration.note: BNE 5$ ;EVERY 16 FRAMES — the comment misstates the cadence; AND I,07 masks 3 bits = every 8 frames. Recorded as a code-vs-comment divergence in open-questions.md.

claim: RESTOR waits for the player-explosion sound (CHAN5) to finish before restoring — the restore animation begins only after the death explosion.

source.verbatim: BNE 5$			;WAIT FOR PLAYER EXPLOSION TO FINISH

claim: RESTOR restores a DAMAGED/POISONED mushroom to a full normal mushroom 0x3F. A cell with (value & 0x3F) in [0x38, 0x3E] is restored to 0x3F; a full mushroom (0x3F) is skipped (BCS 20$ on CMP I,3F); non-mushroom cells (< 0x38) are skipped.

corroboration.note: CMP I,3F / BCS 20$ ;IF FULL MUSHROOM — full mushrooms (0x3F) are not restored; only the 0x38-0x3E partial/poison band is.

claim: RESTOR awards 5 points for each restored mushroom (LDA I,5, added in BCD = 5 points). This matches CENTIP.DOC's 'partial/poisoned mushrooms (after your death) = 5'.

corroboration.note: JSR SCORN1 ;AWARD 5 PTS. FOR RESTORED MUSHROOMS.

claim: The TOP row (vertical index v = 0x1F) is reserved: MUSHER refuses to drop a mushroom there. This is the score/status row at the top of the screen.

corroboration.note: BEQ 20$ ;DON'T PUT UP MUSHROOM IF ON TOP ROW.

claim: The player row (vertical index v = 1) is reserved: MUSHER refuses to drop a mushroom on the same row as the player.

corroboration.note: BEQ 20$ ;NOT ON THE SAME ROW AS THE PLAYER.

claim: A mushroom dropped by a killed centipede segment (MUSHER) is a FULL mushroom 0x3F — the same full value as seeding (PM-10) and RESTOR (PM-25).
MUSHDC decrements the lower-screen mushroom count (MUSH) only when the destroyed mushroom's vertical index is below 0x0C — the same lower/upper boundary the seeding count uses (PM-8).

corroboration.note: 5$: CMP I,0C / BCS 10$ ;IF MUSHROOM IS ON UPPER HALF OF SCREEN — decrement skipped for v >= 0x0C.

claim: Scoring is BCD: SCORN1 sets decimal mode (SED) before adding points, so score constants like 0x01 (mushroom) and 0x05 (restore) add as decimal 1 and 5.
AC-2 diff: CENTIP.DOC (rev-1 design doc) scoring prose says 'Destroying a mushroom = 1'. This AGREES with rev-4 code (PM-20, LDA I,01). No divergence — 1 point is safe to bake.

AC-2 diff: CENTIP.DOC (rev-1) says 'Partial mushrooms or "poisoned" mushrooms (after your death) = 5'. This AGREES with rev-4 RESTOR (PM-26, LDA I,5) and confirms the trigger is the player's death (PM-22). No divergence — 5 points is safe to bake.

AC-2 diff: CENTIP.DOC (rev-1) says 'There will be no mushrooms on the bottom line' (singular). Rev-4 code reserves MORE rows: seeding stays off v=0 AND v=1 (PM-12), and MUSHER also reserves the top score row v=0x1F (PM-27) and the player row v=1 (PM-28). Code wins; the divergence is recorded in open-questions.md.

source.verbatim: scattered throughout the screen.  There will be no mushrooms on the bottom line.
